doctrine: Public predictions, archived BEFORE their outcome date, then measured against what happened. The archive is the product: a claim with a timestamp cannot be quietly edited afterwards. Measured voice only — we record what was claimed and what occurred, never mockery, never a verdict word.

event.name: US Senate cloture vote on the CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633)
event.threshold: 60 votes to proceed to floor debate

hype_claims_observed.claim: +40,000% price move implied around the vote

reference_state_at_archive.note: Prediction-market odds measure the probability of enactment in 2026, not the cloture vote itself. The hype claims conflate the two; that conflation is the specimen.

entries.measurement_plan: On 2026-09-16 publish the outcome card: cloture result (pass/fail, vote count) against the archived hype claims and against the reference odds. The hype is measured against the record, not against the price.

event.name: XRP price at 2030-12-31
sources: short-video social feeds, Sep 2026 (archived by estate observation)

reference_state_at_archive.note: Archived whole, dated, and left standing until the horizon. At $150,000/XRP the implied capitalisation exceeds global M2 — that arithmetic is stated here once, at archive time, not retrofitted in 2030.

entries.measurement_plan: Annual check-in card each December; final outcome card at horizon. No silent edits: this entry's archived_at is its signature content.

event.name: JRE #2551 — Daniel Kokotajlo (AI Futures Project): public incident account of an agentic swarm failure

reference_state_at_archive.note: A mass-audience account of a swarm incident now exists in the public record. What does not exist anywhere public: a measured mapping of that incident class onto named evaluation axes.

entries.measurement_plan: Map the incident class described in the account onto the swarm, jail and detector axes: which axis would have registered the behaviour, at what sample size, with what access. Publish the method and the access-ask. The episode audio itself is not a dataset; access to the incident telemetry is the ask.
entries.access_ask: Incident telemetry or an equivalent replay harness, under NDA if required — measurement, never certification, and the lab keeps veto over publication of anything identifying.
